name: Invest or raise pool cash across mandates
function: Investments (public equities and public market alternatives)
summary: When clients buy or redeem units of a pool, or a mandate is added or terminated, the pool's portfolio managers must invest or raise that cash across the pool's internal sleeves and external manager mandates so the pool stays at its target structure and within its guidelines. An analyst works out the current weights and a draft allocation in a spreadsheet, the portfolio manager decides, larger moves need the managing director, internal orders pass pre-trade compliance on their way to the trading desk, and signed cash notices go to external managers. Most elapsed time is waiting for the dealing date, for managers to trade and for settlement; errors come from stale holdings data, hand-keyed notices and timing mismatches between unit dealing and trading.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about 240 staff running three public equity pools and a public market alternatives pool for five client portfolios, mixing internal strategies and external managers.
baseline.notes: State at end 2021: four pools holding $29.2 billion. Before November 2020 there were no pools, so this process did not exist in 2019.

unit_of_work: one pool cash deployment or raise
trigger: A pool cash flow notice from transfer agency (net subscriptions or redemptions for a pool and dealing date), a new mandate ready for funding, or a transition plan that moves a terminated manager's assets.
end_state: The cash is invested or raised across sleeves and mandates, trades and transfers have settled, the pool is near its target structure and the case is logged; or the flow is withdrawn or netted to nothing.

volume.seasonality: More cases at month end and quarter end, when client contributions, benefit payment funding and rebalancing switches cluster, and in market stress when several clients redeem on the same day.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map: four pools with three to five net flow events a month each.

systems.name: Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Pool unitholder register and transfer agency records (custodian module with controlled spreadsheets)

steps.name: Receive the pool cash flow notice
steps.description: The transfer agency's pool cash flow notice (pool, net subscription or redemption amount, dealing date and settlement date), or a mandate funding or transition request from manager research, lands in the shared mailbox of the pool's portfolio managers. The mailbox rule and the subject line route equity pool items to public equities and public market alternatives items to that team. No one works on it yet.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: Canadian, global or emerging markets equity pool

evidence.note: Four pools at end 2021: three equity pools and the public market alternatives pool. The 82/18 split by case count is the author's estimate; the equity pools held $25.2 billion of the $29.2 billion pooled.

steps.name: Log the flow and pull pool holdings by sleeve and mandate
steps.description: A public equities analyst records the flow in the pool cash flow tracker, pulls the pool's internal sleeve positions from the investment book of record and the external mandate account values from the custodian portal (usually as of the previous day), and calculates each sleeve's and mandate's weight against the pool's target structure, including flows already pending for the same pool.

error.defect_description: Stale or incomplete holdings: a mandate valued a day late or a pending trade left out.

evidence.note: Pools hold internal factor, fundamental and index sleeves next to external mandates. Notices often arrive late in the day and are worked the next morning; wait times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check pool cash, pending settlements and offsetting flows
steps.description: The analyst opens the pool and mandate cash ledgers in the custodian portal and the cash team's forecast to see uninvested cash, unsettled trades, dividends and fees due, and any other flow for the same dealing date. Where one client's redemption offsets another client's subscription, only the net amount needs to be invested or raised.
outputs: net cash to deploy or raise

error.defect_description: An offsetting or pending flow is missed, so too much or too little cash is moved.

evidence.note: Using flows to rebalance and netting them is the low-cost practice the source describes; the netting check itself is the author's description.

steps.name: Draft the allocation across sleeves and mandates
steps.description: In the pool allocation workbook the analyst spreads a subscription toward underweight sleeves and mandates, or draws a redemption first from overweight and most liquid sleeves such as the internal index sleeve, keeping each external account above its minimum size and within the manager's agreed capacity. The workbook shows post-flow weights, residual cash and the change in active risk against the pool benchmark.
inputs: net cash to deploy or raise

error.defect_description: Formula or weight error in the workbook, or a mandate below its minimum size.

evidence.note: A rebalancing policy should set the method for allocating interim cash flows; the specific allocation rules here are the author's estimate of common pool practice.

steps.name: Decide which mandates to fund or draw and when
steps.description: The pool's portfolio manager reviews the draft against current views of each strategy and manager (a manager on watch or under termination gets no new money), decides the split between internal sleeves and external mandates, whether to trade at the dealing-date close to match the unit price or phase a very large flow over several days, and whether to ask the total portfolio team to hold futures exposure on cash in the meantime.

error.defect_description: A manager under review is funded, or a large flow is traded in one day when it should be phased.

next.condition: portfolio manager asks for a different split
flow withdrawn or netted to zero by later instructions

evidence.note: Futures can keep exposure on idle cash while it is raised or awaits investment; choices and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Check the plan against pool guidelines and notice terms
steps.description: The analyst compares the post-flow weights with the ranges in the pool's investment policy statement (strategy and single-manager limits, maximum cash), checks the notice each external manager needs under its agreement, and runs the internal sleeve changes through the order management system's what-if compliance check.

error.defect_description: A range or notice term is misread and the breach is found only after trading.

control.basis: Pool investment policy statement ranges and restrictions; the model manager's OSC exemption order requires board-approved policies that prevent investments contravening the restrictions in each investment management agreement

next.condition: above the portfolio manager's limit or outside target ranges
breach or error found; redo the allocation

evidence.note: Investment policy statements set permitted investments and restrictions for each strategy; the approval threshold share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Managing director approves a large or off-target allocation
steps.description: For a flow above the portfolio manager's delegated limit, or one that leaves a strategy away from its target weight, the managing director of public equities reviews the workbook and the reasons and approves by email or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Delegated authority schedule within the public equities department (author's assumption; the model manager states that approval authorities between the Board, committees and departments are defined)

evidence.note: The model manager publishes that approval authorities are defined but not the thresholds for pool cash allocations; the step and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Split the approved plan into orders and manager instructions
steps.description: The analyst records the final amounts per sleeve and mandate in the tracker, sets the cash to invest or raise in each internal sleeve for the portfolio manager, and lists the external mandates that need a cash notice and transfer.

error.defect_description: An amount is copied wrongly from the approved workbook.

evidence.note: Author's description of a spreadsheet hand-off common where the order system does not hold the pool allocation model.

steps.name: Generate and stage internal sleeve orders in the OMS
steps.description: The portfolio manager runs the order management system's rebalancing tool for each internal index or factor sleeve to buy or sell names in proportion to model weights for the cash amount, removes odd lots and tiny orders, checks the number of names and turnover, and stages the basket of security orders.

error.defect_description: Wrong cash amount or direction entered for a sleeve.

evidence.note: Internal factor and index sleeves are named in the annual report; tool use and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Run pre-trade compliance on the staged basket
steps.description: The order management system checks every staged order against the pool's coded restrictions (restricted list, issuer and ownership limits, prohibited instruments) and either passes the basket or raises warnings or hard blocks.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Condition of the model manager's OSC exemption order: policies and controls that prevent investments contravening the restrictions in each investment management agreement; SOC 1 objective that trades follow portfolio guidelines

evidence.note: Alert rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compliance clears or rejects the pre-trade alert
steps.description: A compliance analyst opens the alert, checks whether it is real or caused by reference data (for example a new security not yet classified), and either records an override with the reason or blocks the order so the portfolio manager amends the basket.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Compliance system under the OSC exemption order: overrides of investment restrictions decided by compliance, not the portfolio manager

evidence.note: The organisation file notes that false alerts from bad reference data take much of compliance's time; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Release the basket to the trading desk
steps.description: On the dealing date the portfolio manager releases the basket to the trading desk in the order management system with instructions: target the close so trading matches the pool's unit price date, or work the orders through the day, and any limits. The orders then belong to trade execution.

error.defect_description: Timing instruction missing, so the basket trades on a different day from the unit dealing date.

next.condition: external mandates also receive or return cash

evidence.note: Wait is the time until the dealing date (often one business day after the notice). Trade execution is a separate process.

steps.name: Draft cash notices to external managers
steps.description: The analyst fills in the manager cash notice template for each mandate: account, currency, amount, add or withdraw, value date and, for withdrawals, the date by which the manager must have cash ready in the custody account.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount, account or value date on a notice.

evidence.note: A public pooled-fund provider asks three to four business days' notice so it can raise or invest cash; manager notice periods in the model manager's agreements are not public (author estimate of one to three business days).

steps.name: Approve and sign manager cash notices
steps.description: The portfolio manager, as an authorised signatory on the manager agreements, checks each notice against the approved allocation and signs it. Notices the manager would not accept, or that do not match, go back to the analyst.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Investment management agreements: managers act only on instructions from authorised signatories named to them

evidence.note: SOC 1 objective that contributions and distributions are authorised and processed accurately; signatory practice is the author's description.

steps.name: Send notices and confirm receipt with each manager
steps.description: The analyst emails the signed notices to each manager's operations contacts with a copy to the custodian relationship team and the cash team, then follows up by email or phone until each manager acknowledges, and marks the tracker.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's description of email-based notice practice in the period.

steps.name: Request transfers between the pool and mandate accounts
steps.description: The analyst sends the cash team transfer requests for the settlement date: from the pool's cash account to each mandate's custody account for a subscription, or from mandate accounts back to the pool account once the managers' sales settle for a redemption, with the notice references.

error.defect_description: Wrong account or value date on a transfer request.

evidence.note: The cash team's dual authorisation of the payment belongs to daily cash management.

steps.name: Trades settle and managers invest or raise cash
steps.description: Internal sleeve trades settle at the custodian two business days after trade date. External managers invest new cash within a few days of receiving it, or sell holdings so that cash is in their custody account by the requested date, and the custodian books the account transfers.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: T+2 settlement in the period; manager response times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check settled positions and residual cash
steps.description: The next morning the analyst checks the custodian and the book of record: transfers booked, internal trades settled at expected amounts, each manager's account shows the cash invested or raised, residual pool cash is within its limit and post-flow weights are close to plan.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: SOC 1 control objective: trades and contributions recorded accurately, completely and timely in the client and pool accounts

next.condition: manager late or short, or unexplained cash difference

evidence.note: Exception share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase a late manager or unexplained cash difference
steps.description: The analyst emails or calls the manager's operations desk or the cash team to find out why cash was not invested or raised as asked (late sales, settlement fail, transfer booked to the wrong account) and agrees a new date.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Review final weights and decide any top-up
steps.description: The portfolio manager reviews the pool's post-flow weights and residual cash and either closes the case or asks for a small top-up rebalance where price moves or partial fills left a sleeve away from target.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Record the deployment and inform operations and total portfolio
steps.description: The analyst completes the tracker with amounts, dates, costs and reasons, files the notices and approvals, and emails unit pricing, investment accounting and the total portfolio team that the flow is fully invested or raised.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Books and records condition of the OSC exemption order and SOC 1 evidence retention

steps.name: Log the flow and model the PMA pool's liquidity
steps.description: A public market alternatives analyst logs the flow and pulls the pool's holdings across managed accounts on the platform, fund investments and the cash and futures sleeve, with each holding's dealing frequency, notice period and any gate, then sketches which holdings can supply or absorb the cash by the dealing date.

error.defect_description: A notice deadline or gate is misread.

evidence.note: The model manager used a managed account platform with 12 managers at end 2021; hedge funds need advance notice for monthly or quarterly redemptions.

steps.name: Decide how to fund or raise the PMA pool flow
steps.description: The PMA portfolio manager decides the sources and uses: the cash sleeve for immediate needs, instructions to managed account managers, subscriptions or redemptions in funds at their next dealing date, and whether a large redemption needs the total portfolio team to meet part of the client's need from other assets.

error.defect_description: A redemption is sized beyond what managed accounts can raise by the date.

next.condition: large flow or change to manager weights

evidence.note: Author estimate of choices and shares.

steps.name: Managing director approves the PMA allocation
steps.description: The managing director of public market alternatives reviews a large or weight-changing allocation, including any fund redemption that crystallises a holdback or a gate, and approves or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Delegated authority schedule within the PMA department (author's assumption)

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare managed account notices and fund dealing requests
steps.description: The analyst drafts cash notices for the managed account managers and, where funds are used, a fund dealing request with fund, class, amount and dealing date for the hedge fund dealing team, which completes the subscription or redemption forms.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount, class or dealing date.

evidence.note: Author estimate; fund dealing itself is a separate process.

steps.name: Sign notices and hand off dealing requests
steps.description: The PMA portfolio manager checks and signs the managed account notices, sends them to the managers and the platform operator, and passes any fund dealing request to the hedge fund dealing process before the fund's notice deadline.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Investment management and platform agreements: instructions only from authorised signatories

steps.name: Request transfers and wait for managed accounts to settle
steps.description: The analyst sends the cash team the transfer requests between the pool account and the managed accounts and waits for the managers to invest or raise cash and the custodian to book the transfers.

error.defect_description: Wrong account on a transfer request.

evidence.note: Wait covers manager trading and T+2 settlement.

steps.name: Confirm the PMA flow is invested or raised and record it
steps.description: The analyst checks the custodian for the transfers and the managed account cash, notes any fund dealing that will settle later, records the case in the tracker and tells unit pricing and the total portfolio team.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: SOC 1 control objective: contributions and distributions processed and recorded accurately

exceptions.name: Large same-day redemptions from several clients
exceptions.description: In market stress several clients redeem at once; the pool raises cash from its most liquid sleeves, the managing director approves, and some managers are asked to sell faster than usual.

exceptions.name: Pre-trade compliance alert
exceptions.description: The staged basket raises a warning or block; compliance overrides a false alert or the portfolio manager amends the basket.

exceptions.name: Manager late or short
exceptions.description: A manager has not invested or raised the cash by the date, or a transfer went to the wrong account; the analyst chases and rechecks.

exceptions.name: New mandate funding
exceptions.description: A newly onboarded mandate is funded by drawing from the internal index sleeve or other mandates rather than from a client flow.

exceptions.name: Manager termination and transition
exceptions.description: Assets of a terminated manager are moved in kind to a transition manager or another mandate and the proceeds reallocated; currency exposure is hedged in the meantime.

exceptions.name: Hedge fund dealing needed
exceptions.description: Part of a PMA pool flow is met by fund subscriptions or redemptions at the funds' next dealing dates, handed to hedge fund dealing.

exceptions.name: Flow withdrawn or netted
exceptions.description: Later instructions offset the flow before any trade is made.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the pool cash flow notice to the logged, settled deployment
benchmarks.population: Daily-dealt institutional equity and alternatives pools mixing internal sleeves and external mandates

evidence.note: No published measure. Built from one to two days to the dealing date, T+2 settlement, one to three days for managers to trade and a day to check; a peer pooled-fund provider settles on the third business day after notice.

benchmarks.unit: business days of notice for withdrawals (four for contributions)
benchmarks.population: Minnesota State Board of Investment non-retirement pooled funds, 2024 procedures

evidence.note: Analog only; the model manager's pool notice terms are not public.

benchmarks.unit: share of U.S. manager transitions in 2015 with a delay or implementation period of one to 12 months
benchmarks.population: State Street research cited by MJ Hudson

evidence.note: Applies to the transition trigger, not ordinary pool flows.

pain_points.description: Notices often arrive late in the day before the dealing date, leaving little time to plan, approve and stage orders, so work spills into the dealing morning.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: External mandate values come from the custodian a day late and the allocation model lives in a spreadsheet outside the order system, so figures are re-keyed between tools.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Unit dealing, trade settlement and manager trading run on different dates, so cash sits uninvested or exposure is short for days unless an overlay holds exposure.
False pre-trade compliance alerts from incomplete security reference data hold up baskets on the dealing date.

evidence.note: Organisation file description of investment compliance monitoring.

pain_points.description: Hedge fund notice periods and gates make the PMA pool slow to raise cash.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Three equity pools and the public market alternatives pool ($29.2 billion pooled at end 2021); pooling brings operational efficiencies in day-to-day pool activities and cash management; public equities combine internal fundamental, factor (size, quality, value, momentum) and index strategies with external managers; fixed income ($17.2 billion) is managed internally for capital preservation and liquidity against FTSE Canada government indices; global credit ($6.0 billion) does not separate public and private credit, plans to internalise through direct co-investments, invested US$500 million with Antares (sponsor-backed middle-market direct lending) and US$500 million with Ares; PMA uses a managed account platform with 12 managers; Investment Policy Statements per strategy set permitted investments and restrictions; Management Investment Committee and three Investment Department Committees (Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit, Real Assets) approve up to thresholds; clean SOC 1 Type I report at 30 September 2021.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemption order)
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. The model manager exempted from adviser registration on conditions; Board-approved policies must cover a compliance system, books and records, conflicts including front running, soft dollars and fairness in allocating investment opportunities among members and pools, prevention of investments that contravene restrictions set out in each investment management agreement, due diligence on sub-advisers, and due diligence on custodians and brokers before they hold or access assets.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Baseline SOC 1 control objectives: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded in accordance with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; contributions and distributions authorised by the client and processed accurately; other control areas include brokerage allocation (best execution, soft dollars, IPO and new issue allocation), broker selection and retention, trade aggregation, trade allocation, trade errors and guideline breaches.

sources.title: Accelerating the U.S. Securities Settlement Cycle to T+1
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Settlement cycle of trade date plus two days (T+2) in the period; about 20% of institutional allocations occur during the trading day and 80% after the close on trade date; confirmation and affirmation can only start once allocations are complete.

sources.title: Rebalancing 2004
sources.supports: Using cash flows such as contributions or redemptions to move portfolios toward target can almost eliminate the marginal cost of rebalancing; a rebalancing policy should document triggers, the method for allocating interim cash flows and the procedure for raising or holding cash, with clear responsibility; hedge funds and absolute return strategies are only semi-liquid and need advance notice for monthly, quarterly or annual redemptions; costs include commissions, spreads, market impact, time and resources.

sources.title: Revisiting the Discussion About Futures-Based Portfolio Overlays
sources.supports: Futures overlays keep beta exposure on idle cash awaiting withdrawal and keep risk allocations at target while cash is raised; overlay managers can take a direct custodian feed and rebalance the next day; implementation of an overlay programme takes about six to eight weeks.

sources.title: Trusts and Other Participating Entities: Procedures (2024)
sources.supports: A public pooled-fund provider asks for four business days' advance notice of contributions and at least three business days' notice of withdrawals; transactions settle on the third business day after notification if received before 2:00 PM; same-day trades are not allowed; trades of one million dollars or more need prior notice for internal control.

sources.title: BCI Pooled Funds - Structure & Performance
sources.supports: Peer provincial manager: assets held in trust with clients holding units of pooled funds; public market pools open daily and private market pools typically annually; unit price is market value divided by units outstanding; the board approves pooled fund investment policies.

sources.title: Top Ten Tips For Transition Management
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Delays between a decision to change managers and implementation are an unmanaged risk; implementation shortfall is the standard cost measure; target managers are not always best placed to run a transition; currency exposure should be hedged during a transition; footnote: 70% of U.S. transitions in 2015 had a delay or implementation period of one to 12 months (State Street research).

assumptions: The model manager has not published how its pool managers deploy flows; steps follow common multi-manager pool practice and peer documents, and most times and probabilities are tier C estimates.

Volume is the organisation file's 5 to 16 to 30 cases a month: net flows per pool per dealing date after netting, plus mandate fundings and transitions; one case may cover several mandates and an internal basket of many security orders.
Trade execution, cash payments with dual authorisation, hedge fund dealing and transition management are separate processes; this workflow ends at their hand-off or waits for their results.
Equity pool cases are worked by public equities analysts and portfolio managers; PMA cases by the PMA team. The 82/18 split is an estimate.
The compliance analyst role is added to the process map's roles because pre-trade alerts need an independent reviewer; the time is small.
Approval thresholds for the managing directors are assumed; the model manager states only that approval authorities are defined.
Loaded costs per hour come from the organisation file (estimated total pay for investment professionals, loading 1.35).
The cycle time benchmark is an estimate; the simulated median is compared with it.
